skill.name: test-generator
skill.description: Generate Python pytest boilerplate for functions, classes, asynchronous code, parametrized cases, and fixtures while following documented project conventions.
skill.summary: Create structured pytest test files with type hints, docstrings, fixtures, parametrization, and Arrange-Act-Assert sections.
skill.author: Atyantik

content.value_statement: Writing consistent pytest files manually is repetitive and can miss project conventions. This skill builds structured boilerplate from source signatures and documented TDD rules.
actual_capabilities: Reads project documentation and source signatures before preparing tests.
Creates pytest structures for functions, classes, asynchronous functions, and parametrized cases.
Produces fixture templates with setup, yield, and teardown sections.
Organizes tests with type hints, docstrings, and Arrange-Act-Assert sections.
Suggests happy paths, edge cases, invalid inputs, and exception scenarios.
Summarizes generated test classes, functions, fixtures, and recommended next steps.
limitations: The included templates target Python and pytest rather than other languages or test frameworks.
Generated cases contain TODO placeholders and require project-specific data and assertions.
Behavior and coverage cannot be verified without accessible source code and project documentation.
The package does not include the referenced exception template or generator script.

use_cases.title: Start Tests for a New Function
use_cases.description: Generate typed pytest cases for normal inputs, boundaries, and expected exceptions before implementation begins.

use_cases.title: Standardize Team Test Files
use_cases.description: Apply shared naming, docstring, import, fixture, and Arrange-Act-Assert conventions across a project.

use_cases.title: Expand Existing Test Coverage
use_cases.description: Identify public behaviors and prepare parametrized, asynchronous, and error-focused test structures for review.

prompt_templates.title: Generate Function Tests
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate pytest tests for {function_name} in {source_file}. Cover normal input, one boundary case, and one invalid input.
prompt_templates.scenario: Create an initial test file for one function.

prompt_templates.title: Generate Class Tests
prompt_templates.prompt: Read {source_file} and generate tests for {class_name}. Include an instance fixture, initialization checks, method behavior, and error cases.
prompt_templates.scenario: Build structured coverage for a class and its public methods.

prompt_templates.title: Generate Async Tests
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate pytest tests for the asynchronous function {function_name}. Include success, dependency failure, timeout, and concurrent execution scenarios.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Module Test Suite
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze {source_file} and project testing rules. Generate focused tests for every public behavior using fixtures and parametrization where appropriate. Explain remaining TODO items.
prompt_templates.scenario: Prepare a comprehensive, convention-aligned module test suite.

output_examples.input: Generate tests for a validate_email function that returns true for valid addresses and raises ValueError for empty input.
output: Created a validator test class with normal, malformed, empty, whitespace, and boundary cases.
Grouped repeated email examples into parametrized cases.
Left project-specific import paths and uncommon domain rules for review.

output_examples.input: Generate tests for an asynchronous fetch_data function with timeout handling.
output: Created asynchronous success, timeout, service-error, and concurrent-call test scenarios.
Used pytest-asyncio markers and isolated the external HTTP dependency.
Listed response fixtures and expected exceptions that require project-specific values.

output_examples.input: Generate tests for a UserManager class with create, delete, and find methods.
output: Created an instance fixture and initialization checks.
Added focused cases for creation, deletion, search results, duplicates, and missing users.
Suggested parametrization for repeated search criteria and explicit cleanup behavior.

best_practices: Provide the source file and relevant project testing conventions.
Replace every TODO with concrete inputs, expected values, and meaningful assertions.
Run generated tests before implementation, then review failures and coverage after each change.
anti_patterns: Do not accept placeholder assertions as completed behavioral tests.
Do not mock internal application logic when real execution is practical.
Do not generate broad tests that combine unrelated behaviors in one case.

faq.question: Which language and framework does this skill support?
faq.answer: It provides templates and guidance for Python tests written with pytest.

faq.question: Can it generate tests for asynchronous functions?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes pytest-asyncio patterns for basic and concurrent asynchronous behavior.

faq.question: Does it create complete production-ready tests?
faq.answer: No. Generated boilerplate includes TODO items that require real data, expected results, and project-specific assertions.

faq.question: Can it generate reusable fixtures?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes a fixture template with typed setup, yield, and teardown sections.

faq.question: Will it run tests or measure coverage automatically?
faq.answer: No automatic runner is included. The guidance recommends project commands for testing, formatting, and coverage.

faq.question: What project context should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide source files, dependency behavior, expected exceptions, testing conventions, and any coverage requirements.
